Author: chefboyrdave2.1
Message:
fix(call): resolve the group-call caller from the seat the group carries (#116)

The operator's own group-call routes computed their caller identity from the
hardcoded OPERATOR_ID constant: _group_caller_uri returned "chef@skworld.io"
from BOTH of its branches, so the membership lookup it appeared to perform had
no effect. Meanwhile guest_groups.create_dm_invite seeds a fresh dm/gdm group's
operator seat from identity_bridge.get_sovereign_identity(), the running
agent's identity, which on the live daemon is capauth:lumina@skworld.io.

The two only agreed when the daemon literally ran as chef@skworld.io. Under the
documented default (skchat-daemon.service runs the lumina agent) they diverged
and POST /v1/groups/{gid}/call/join answered 403 "not a member of this group",
locking the operator out of a gdm room their own guests were sitting in. That
is the "3-party call unverified" follow-up from the guest-dm invites epic.

_group_caller_uri now returns whichever identity is actually on the roster,
resolved across the daemon's own identities only (_local_call_identities: the
operator constant plus the running agent). It is deliberately NOT "whatever
holds the admin seat": that would let this daemon mint a publish-capable
LiveKit token under a REMOTE peer's identity for any group that peer created.
When no local identity is a member the caller stays OPERATOR_ID so the gate
still fails closed. Both /call/start and /call/join share the helper.

Tests: new server-level suite drives the real FastAPI routes and decodes the
minted LiveKit JWTs, proving operator + 2 web guests land in one room, guest
tokens stay room/identity scoped (never admin or recorder), cross-room guests
are refused, and revoked guests get no token. The operator-join case landed as
a strict xfail documenting the bug and is now a passing regression test, plus a
guard that a remote peer's seat is never adopted (verified red-green: the naive
admin-seat version fails it).

Author: Lumina
Message:
feat(guest): guest-dm G7 (server) - a gdm ring reaches a ws-less operator

C5 gave the operator a poll fallback for guest call rings, but only ever
stamped the ring onto the mode=dm badge. On a PROMOTED room a ws-less operator
therefore got nothing at all: the guest pressed call and it rang into silence.

A gdm is not just a dm with more people, so the flat ringing/ring_ts pair is not
enough to answer with - several guests share the room, and the operator has to
know which one is calling. `ringers` names them, newest first, resolved from the
operator's own dm_contacts row (alias-wins, same rule as the roster) and never
from anything the guest supplies, so the banner cannot be made to render a name
a guest picked for themselves. ring_ts stays as the newest ring so the existing
client dedupe key keeps working unchanged.

Only seated members are considered, so a revoked guest stops ringing the moment
they leave the roster - answering their ring would join nobody.

8 tests, including the two file-sharing rules a promoted room implies (the other
guest in the room can read an upload; a revoked guest is refused with a 403, not
a 404 pretending the file never existed). Both already held; they are pinned here
so the gdm sharing contract cannot regress silently.

Stacks on G6 (feat/guest-dm-g6-server-roster) and on the C5 ring poll fallback
(feat/guest-dm-c5-server-ring-pollfallback, PR #110), both merged in here.

Message:
test(guest-dm): G-E2E - server integration suite for the group extension (G1-G4)

Hand-rolled the group half of the guest-DM E2E gate (epic 8685ede6), in the
style of the merged 1:1 suite test_guest_dm_e2e.py. 8 independent scenarios:
- promotion: a dm flips to gdm IN PLACE (same group id), posts the
  dm_promoted_to_gdm system notice, admits a second per-person guest behind the
  epoch fence (no pre-promotion history), keeps guest A's session working, and
  enforces the gdm seat cap (SKCHAT_GDM_SEAT_CAP).
- shared link: one reusable link admits N distinct browser keys into ONE group,
  dedupes a returning key, and disabling the link (revoking its jti) blocks new
  joins without locking out already-admitted guests.
- files + calls: a gdm guest's file is downloadable by the other guest, a
  foreign transfer id 403/404s, both guests get a call token for the SAME
  derived room, the ring reaches the operator over the ws broadcast, and a muted
  contact's ring is silent.
- revoke: per-group revoke kills only that membership (reason membership_revoked)
  while the person's separate 1:1 DM keeps working; person-level revoke kills
  everything (reason contact_revoked).

Autopilot repeatedly died after the run banner on this card (card-specific;
the sibling 1:1 E2E built fine), so this was written bare-metal. All 8 pass.

Message:
feat(guest-dm): C5 server - guest-call ring POLL FALLBACK for ws-less clients

S6 rings the operator over a ws broadcast, but skworld-app has no ws channel
(it polls /call/incoming). This adds a transient poll fallback so the poll-only
app can raise an incoming-ring banner:

- guest_groups: an in-memory, TTL'd ring registry keyed by guest fp
  (mark_guest_ringing / guest_ring_ts / clear_guest_ring). In-memory on purpose:
  a ring is ephemeral (45s TTL, self-pruning), never worth a schema migration,
  and a restart cancelling a stale ring is correct.
- guest_group_routes._ring_operator_for_guest_call: stamps the ring alongside
  the existing ws broadcast. Muted contacts already return early, so a muted
  guest never stamps a ring.
- daemon_proxy_groups._dm_guest_badge: surfaces ringing:bool + ring_ts on the
  operator group/conversation payload (/api/v1/conversations), which the app
  already polls, so the client dedupes by ring_ts and decides freshness.
- 3 tests: registry mark/read/expire/clear, operator payload reflects a live
  ring after a guest call, muted guest never stamps a ring. No regressions
  across the S6 ring + contact-route suites.

Client leg (guest-ring watcher + banner + answer) lands in the skworld-app C5 PR.

Author: Lumina
Message:
feat(spaces): M1b participant trust badges via PROVEN-identity token metadata

Extends the M1b trust badge to conf/Space/call participants. Each participant's
capauth soul_fingerprint is embedded in the LiveKit token participant-metadata at
mint, parsed client-side, and rendered as the same red/amber TrustBadge as 1:1 +
group. Unspoofable because no participant role carries can_update_own_metadata.

SECURITY (adversarial-review-driven): the fingerprint is stamped ONLY from a
cryptographically-PROVEN identity, never a caller-supplied one. An earlier draft
stamped it on the public /conf/{room}/token and /spaces/{id}/join routes, where
identity is unauthenticated -- a spoof (any caller could POST identity=lumina and
wear her badge). Corrected model:
  - STAMP on proven paths: join_routes /join/sovereign and spaces federation
    authd (both after verify_signed of the fqid), and conf federated-token.
  - NO stamp on unproven/public paths: conf create-host, /conf/{room}/token join,
    /spaces/{id}/join, and the gated-but-caller-chosen /livekit/token.
  - fingerprint_for_identity is now STRICT (full identity/handle/fqid only, no
    bare short-name), closing a cross-realm collision where a remote
    artisan@opB could inherit the LOCAL artisan's key.
  - moderation StageState round-trips soul_fingerprint so a hand-raise/invite no
    longer clobbers it (set_sharing already passes metadata verbatim).

Tests: mint embeds metadata; proven /join/sovereign + federation authd stamp;
public conf/space join do NOT stamp (regression guards for the exact attack);
strict resolution rejects bare/cross-realm short-names; moderation round-trip
preserves the fingerprint. Full suite 2863 pass (pre-existing e2e/integration
live-stack failures unchanged).

Message:
docs(bootstrap): node identity + agent-home bootstrap chain (Task 6)

Documents the ordered dependency chain for a blank machine to join the
skchat plane (skenv install -> CapAuth identity/PGP import -> skvault
unlock -> ~/.skchat restore -> systemd install --enable -> tailscale
ingress), calling out exactly where the skvault chicken-and-egg breaks:
skvault unlock requires the operator's private key already present in
the local gpg keyring, so the key import must happen out-of-band before
skvault is ever invoked. Also documents the identity.json/~/.skcomms/peers
gap left by the Task-1 backup (both live outside ~/.skchat and are needed
for a full restore).

scripts/bootstrap-node.sh runs the chain with per-step preflight checks,
idempotent re-runs, and a --check dry-run mode that performs no mutation.

Author: Lumina
Message:
fix(livekit): hand off-tailnet Funnel callers the public SFU URL

The public-aware SFU URL selection was host-header based, which is broken on
the .158 Tailscale Funnel deployment: the public Funnel URL and the tailnet
URL share a hostname and differ only by PORT (wss://noroc2027.tail204f0c.ts.net
on public :443 vs :8443 on the tailnet). _request_host strips the port, so the
Host was identical for both and the helper always returned :8443, which a
cellular phone can never reach. Every off-tailnet call/conf join was dead
before TURN even mattered.

Reconcile public_aware_livekit_url with the robust off-tailnet detection used
by /connectivity/ice (call_routes): honor the Tailscale-Funnel-Request ingress
signal and the real client IP (X-Forwarded-For when the socket peer is a
loopback proxy). A Funnel-proxied guest is now handed the public wss URL even
when its Host header looks tailnet; genuine tailnet/LAN/loopback callers keep
the :8443 fast path. Host-header discrimination is retained as a fallback for
name-split deployments.

The IP/funnel helpers (_ONTAILNET_NETS, _parse_ip, _real_client_ip) now live in
livekit_routes as the single source of truth; call_routes imports them so the
two paths cannot drift.

Made the remaining raw-URL public paths public-aware too: /join/sovereign,
/conf/{room}/federated-token, and the SK Spaces token responses + /sfu/get
(guest/host/listener joins). Routes already calling the helper (/guest/join,
guest group call, /conf token via _public_url, group A/V call) are fixed by the
helper change. The operator-token gate on /livekit/token is untouched. Server
to SFU HTTP calls (roster/list_participants) correctly keep the tailnet URL.

Tests: 7 new cases in test_public_url proving a Funnel-proxied off-tailnet
guest-join and conf-token get the wss://.../livekit-ws public URL (not :8443)
while a genuine tailnet peer with the same hostname still gets :8443. 234
targeted tests green.

Author: Lumina
Message:
calls: Phase 3 backend — group A/V call endpoints (start/join/participants)

On-the-fly group video + screenshare on the LiveKit SFU, over the WEB HTTP
path (the Flutter app is a web build — CLI is a no-op). Backs the new
daemon-proxy endpoints with the Phase-2 group membership + the LiveKit token
mint:

* daemon_proxy_groupcall.py — deterministic per-group room
  (derive_group_room: "gcall-" + 16 base32, opaque hash so the group id never
  hits the SFU's room logs), member-scoped token mint (publish+subscribe+data,
  never room_admin; non-members refused with PermissionError), and a group
  ring that reuses the 1:1 CALL_INVITE envelope (tagged with group_id) so
  members get the existing /call/incoming surface.
* daemon_proxy.py — POST /api/v1/groups/{id}/call/start (mint + ring),
  /call/join (mint, no ring), GET /call/participants (SFU ListParticipants,
  degrades to roster-only when the SFU is unreachable, never 500).
* Membership gate everywhere: 403 non-member, 404 unknown group, 503 livekit
  unconfigured.
* Recording seam (Phase 6) exposed but inert: group_call_context returns a
  recording_hook {room} — the documented attach point for a future LiveKit
  Egress. No egress started here.

9 new tests (test_daemon_proxy_groupcall.py): deterministic room, room does
not leak group id, member-only token mint with room-scoped grant, start mints
token + rings everyone-but-caller, ring:false suppresses ring, join never
rings, 404/503 gates, participants endpoint. Existing group/call/livekit-gate
tests unchanged. (6 pre-existing failures in test_conf_agent/test_agent_profile
are unrelated to this change.)

The conf federation SERVER route POST /conf/{room}/federated-token was live but
had no client caller, so Shape-A ("sovereign") cross-instance conf join had never
run E2E. This adds the missing client leg, mirroring the audio Space federation

  fqid=...) builds a capauth-signed FQID assertion ({claim, sig}) via the shared
  assertion.build_signed path and POSTs it to the remote conf authd. Returns the
  server payload {token, url, role, identity, conf_id, room}. POST + sign seams
  injectable for testing. ConfAuthDenied(403) / ConfFederationError(404, non-2xx).
- src/skchat/cli.py: `skchat conf join-federated --host <remote> --room <room>
  [--fqid ...] [--json]` — mints + prints the token + SFU url for app/browser use.
- tests/test_conf_fed_client.py: sign->POST(mock)->parse round-trip + error paths,
  AND real client->server round-trips via FastAPI TestClient (no verify/trust/mint
  mocks): trusted+pinned fqid mints a real LiveKit JWT; untrusted fqid -> 403.

Message:
conf: pull the Lumina AI agent into a conf room on demand (34bd409b)

Add host-gated POST /conf/{room}/invite-agent + /conf/{room}/remove-agent to
the Sovereign Conf Calls API. invite-agent launches the Lumina LiveKit agent
(lumina-creative/scripts/lumina-call.py — a DIFFERENT repo, NOT modified) into
the given room as a transient, supervised, resource-scoped systemd --scope unit:

  systemd-run --user --scope --unit=lumina-conf-<sanitized-room> \
    --property=MemoryMax=2G --property=CPUQuota=200% \
    <SKCHAT_AGENT_PYTHON> <SKCHAT_LUMINA_CALL_SCRIPT> \
    --room <room> --greet "<greeting>"

The agent self-mints its LiveKit token over the loopback WEBUI_URL/livekit/token
gate. The room name is sanitized into the unit name (alnum/dash only) to prevent
argument injection. Script path + python are env-overridable
(SKCHAT_LUMINA_CALL_SCRIPT / SKCHAT_AGENT_PYTHON), defaulting to the known paths.

Teardown: /conf/{room}/end and /conf/{room}/remove-agent both best-effort
`systemctl --user stop lumina-conf-<room>.scope`. Degrades gracefully (clear
503/502, never a crash) when systemd-run is missing or the spawn fails.

The systemd-run/systemctl runner is injectable (runner= on register_conf_routes,
defaults to a real subprocess.run) so tests assert the command shape and teardown
without ever spawning a process. Touches only conf/routes.py + a new test.

Author: Lumina
Message:
conf: public-aware SFU endpoint URL (df42e2a4)

Make the LiveKit SFU URL handed to the browser request-aware so a public
guest arriving via Tailscale Funnel gets a PUBLIC wss URL while tailnet
clients keep the tailnet :8443 URL.

New env SKCHAT_LIVEKIT_PUBLIC_URL (public/Funnel-reachable wss URL).
Detection: if the public url is set AND the request Host / X-Forwarded-Host
does NOT match the tailnet host (derived from SKCHAT_LIVEKIT_URL's hostname,
or explicit SKCHAT_TAILNET_HOST), return the public url; otherwise tailnet.
No host header (local caller) -> tailnet. Public url unset -> always tailnet
(byte-for-byte backward compatible).

Shared helper public_aware_livekit_url(request) in livekit_routes.py, used by
all three URL-handing sites:
  - GET  /livekit/config
  - POST /livekit/token
  - POST /guest/join (guest.py, with defensive fallback to the tailnet default)

Tests: tests/test_public_url.py (13) — helper unit cases (public/tailnet/
no-host/X-Forwarded-Host/explicit-host/no-public) + /livekit/config,
/livekit/token and /guest/join integration via FastAPI TestClient.

Author: Lumina
Message:
spaces: add CONFERENCE video role→grant tier (sovereign conf calls)

Audio Spaces today are mic-only (SPEAKER = ["microphone"], no camera/screen)
and the guest builder strips screenshare. Conf calls need camera + mic +
screenshare with guests still denied admin. Adds a parallel conf role family
WITHOUT touching the load-bearing audio HOST/SPEAKER/LISTENER semantics.

roles.py
- New `ConfRole` enum: PARTICIPANT / PRESENTER / SOVEREIGN / AGENT / GUEST_CONF.
- `RoleGrant` gains room_record / room_destroy flags (default False; audio roles
  never set them).
- Single grant factory `conf_grant_for(role, space_id, *, sovereign_admin=False)`:
    PARTICIPANT/PRESENTER/SOVEREIGN/GUEST_CONF → can_publish_sources =
      ["camera","microphone","screen_share","screen_share_audio"]
    AGENT → ["microphone"] only (+ data + subscribe), no admin (Lumina-in-call)
    SOVEREIGN → optional room_admin via sovereign_admin flag
    GUEST_CONF → hard-guarded: room_admin/room_record/room_destroy forced False
  This is the one chokepoint so no caller can over-grant admin to a guest.
- Verified LiveKit TrackSource enum strings against livekit-api 1.1.0
  (livekit/protocol/models.pyi): microphone / camera / screen_share /
  screen_share_audio, serialized verbatim into video.canPublishSources.

tokens.py
- `mint_conf_token(...)` routes through conf_grant_for and maps room_record onto
  the LiveKit VideoGrant. Shared `_video_grants_from` / `_build_token` helpers;
  `mint_space_token` behavior unchanged.

guest.py
- `build_livekit_token` gains optional `allow_screenshare=False`. Default path is
  byte-for-byte unchanged (camera+microphone only). When True, the source set +
  admin denial come from conf_grant_for(GUEST_CONF, ...) so a conf guest may
  share screen but is never room_admin/room_record. Route registration /
  InviteIssuer untouched.

tests: table-driven assertions — conf roles include screen_share; GUEST_CONF
never admin/record/destroy (even with sovereign_admin=True); AGENT mic+data only;
audio SPEAKER stays mic-only (no regression); default guest token has no
screenshare, conf guest token does. 71 passed.

Author: Lumina
Message:
feat(spaces): local sovereign conf join (POST /join/sovereign)

Add a LOCAL (non-federation) capauth-proven conference join. Until now,
assertion-verified token minting only existed behind the federation
route /sfu/get (spaces.federation.authd.authorize), which is built for
remote peers (per-FQID TrustPolicy, audio Space, speaker/listener cap).

POST /join/sovereign is the local analog for conference video: the
client signs an Assertion{fqid, space_id, nonce} with its capauth key
(reuse federation.assertion.build_signed); the endpoint verifies via
assertion.verify_signed + the replay-nonce guard (federation.nonce),
then mints a SOVEREIGN-grant conf token (tokens.mint_conf_token,
role=ConfRole.SOVEREIGN) using the PROVEN fqid as the LiveKit identity
— never a caller-supplied string. room_admin is opt-in via
sovereign_admin and only honored for SOVEREIGN inside conf_grant_for.

Mirrors authd.authorize structurally (verify -> replay -> mint) with a
local trust policy: a valid self-signature over the claimed fqid is
sufficient proof for a sovereign joining their own conference (no remote
allowlist to consult).

- new src/skchat/join_routes.py (authorize_sovereign + register_join_routes)
- webui.py: register the route (guarded import, mirrors spaces/guest)
- tests/test_join_sovereign.py: proven-identity + SOVEREIGN grant
  (camera+screen sources), replay rejected, bad signature rejected,
  tampered fqid rejected, route 400/200 mapping (9 tests)

Author: Lumina
Message:
feat: swap Lumina TTS from VoxCPM to F5-TTS

After A/B-testing voice clone fidelity against the same Jessica
reference WAV across three TTS engines:
- VoxCPM: best timbre but 5-15GB VRAM (leaks), 1.5x realtime
- XTTS-v2: 5x faster but 'similar but not as good' (Chef's words)
- F5-TTS: 'pretty close' to VoxCPM (Chef approved), 0.75GB VRAM,
  3x faster sustained throughput, ~1.4s TTFB

Pointing skchat-lumina-call.service env at F5 endpoint
(http://skworld-100:18796/audio/speech).

VoxCPM stays running on port 18793 as a fallback. F5's CC-BY-NC
license is fine for personal/research use; if AI LIFE goes
commercial we'd need to re-train F5 on commercial-OK data or fall
back to VoxCPM (Apache-2 weights).

Net wins:
- VRAM: 8.8 GB freed → MuseTalk fits back on .100 alongside F5+Ollama
- VRAM leak: solved (F5 stable at 0.75 GB)
- Multi-sentence replies: synth gap drops from ~3s to ~1s

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>
